source: Curated from public announcements, news reports, and EPA Brownfields documentation. Refresh annually.

campuses.name: Google Widows Creek Data Center
campuses.previous_use: TVA Widows Creek Fossil Plant (coal, retired 2015)
campuses.notes: Built on 360 ac of a 2,000-ac TVA site; powered by dedicated solar/renewables via TVA PPA; campus expanded to 2+ buildings.

campuses.name: Aligned Data Centers Conesville AI Campus
campuses.previous_use: AEP Conesville Power Plant (coal, 2,005 MW, retired April 2020)
campuses.notes: Multi-billion-dollar phased campus; first DC delivery expected mid-2026; PJM interconnect inherited from plant retirement; Coshocton County.

campuses.name: Homer City Energy Campus
campuses.previous_use: Homer City Generating Station (coal, 2,000 MW, PA's largest; retired July 2023)
campuses.notes: 4.4 GW new natural gas plant (7x GE Vernova hydrogen-capable turbines) + co-located hyperscale DC campus; dual PJM + NYISO interconnect; ~10,000 construction jobs; first gas power ~2027–2028.

campuses.name: AWS Susquehanna Nuclear Campus
campuses.previous_use: Buffer land adjacent to Susquehanna Steam Electric Station (2.5 GW nuclear, operational); campus carved from nuclear plant buffer zone.
campuses.notes: AWS acquired campus from Talen Energy for $650M; 17-year 1.92 GW nuclear PPA signed 2025 through 2042; 1,200-ac campus; FERC blocked direct behind-the-fence co-location but PPA approved. Note: nuclear plant remains operational (not brownfield).

campuses.name: NorthPoint Keystone Trade Center DC Campus
campuses.previous_use: U.S. Steel Fairless Works (integrated steel mill, 1952–2011; 2,200-ac total site)
campuses.notes: 10 DC buildings (~2M sqft total) on 247-ac phase of 1,850-ac master site; legacy industrial microgrid with >2,000 MW capacity; Bucks County. Keystone NAP colocation (2 MW, operational) already on-site.

campuses.name: Project Marvel AI Campus
campuses.previous_use: Former U.S. Steel timberlands / industrial land (Valley Creek Land & Timber, acquired from U.S. Steel 2015)
campuses.notes: 18 buildings; 4.5M sqft; 673 ac rezoned (additional 900 ac sought); near I-459/I-20/59 interchange; 2M gal/day water from Warrior River; hyperscale tenant under NDA. Jefferson County.

campuses.name: Meta Forest City Data Center Campus
campuses.previous_use: Burlington Industries textile mill (1970s–1990s), then Tracker Marine manufacturing; vacant 2008; formal NC Brownfields Agreement 2012.
campuses.notes: First campus online 2012; now 1.3M sqft across 3 buildings; EPA brownfields assessment funds used for site cleanup; Meta is largest single tax contributor to Rutherford County (~14% of county revenue).

campuses.name: QTS Richmond Data Center Campus
campuses.previous_use: Qimonda DRAM semiconductor fab (300mm wafer fab, bankrupt 2009); QTS acquired via bankruptcy auction 2010 for $12M.
campuses.notes: Richmond 1: 1.3M sqft, 110 MW; 2024 expansion: 622-ac White Oak Technology Park (Richmond 2+3). Strongest semiconductor-fab-to-DC precedent in the US.

campuses.name: Cheswick Generation Station DC Site
campuses.previous_use: Cheswick Generation Station (coal, along Allegheny River, demolished prior to sale)
campuses.notes: 47-ac riverfront parcel acquired Nov 2025 for $14.3M; 180 MW planned; Allegheny County. Compact coal-to-DC conversion.

campuses.name: Microsoft Project Fairwater AI Data Center
campuses.previous_use: Foxconn LCD factory site (planned 2017; partially built; never fully operational as fab; stranded industrial infrastructure)
campuses.notes: $3.3B Phase 1 + $4B+ additional approved Jan 2026; 15 buildings approved; Racine County; reuses stranded Foxconn high-voltage electrical infrastructure. Quasi-brownfield (stranded industrial, not contaminated).
